source.title: Some Open Problems Concerning Expansive Systems

accepted.question_text: Let T^2 be the two-torus and let f: T^2 -> T^2 be an expansive diffeomorphism. Must f belong to the C^1-closure of the set of Anosov diffeomorphisms on T^2? Equivalently, is every expansive diffeomorphism of the two-torus a C^1-limit of Anosov diffeomorphisms?
accepted.context_brief: Approximation of expansive torus diffeomorphisms by Anosov maps

evidence.quote: However, it is not known, whether the C1-closure of the C1-interior of the expansive diffeomorphisms of T2 includes all the expansive diffeomorphisms of the 2-torus. In other words: Is every expansive diffeomorphism the C1-limit of Anosov diffeomorphisms?
Open Problem 10.1: Does the C1-closure of the set of Anosov diffeomorphisms contains all expansive diffeomorphisms of the two-Torus?

accepted.question_text: Let f be an expansive homeomorphism of a compact metric space M. Say that the semi-trajectory of a point x is persistent in the future if for every epsilon > 0 there exists a C^0-neighborhood N_x of f such that, for every g in N_x, there is y in M with dist(f^n(x), g^n(y)) <= epsilon for all n >= 0; define persistence in the past analogously for n <= 0. Is every semi-trajectory of every expansive system persistent in the future and in the past?
accepted.context_brief: Persistence of semi-trajectories in expansive systems

evidence.quote: However each semi-trajectory is persistent : given x ∈ M, and ε > 0 there is, Nx, a C0-neighbourhood of f such that for any g ∈ Nx, there is y ∈ M, with the property dist(f^n(x), g^n(y)) ≤ ε, n ≥ 0. This is the f persistence of x in the future. We define similarly persistence in the past. ... An open question is: are all the semi-trajectories of an expansive system persistent?
Open Problem 10.2: For an Expansive Homeomorphism is every semi-trajectory peristent in the future (in the past)?

accepted.question_text: Consider the map f: T^2 -> T^2 defined by f(x, y) = (2x + y - (c/(2π)) sin(2πx), x + y - (c/(2π)) sin(2πx)). For parameter values c > 1, does this map have positive Lyapunov exponents on a set of positive measure?
accepted.context_brief: Lyapunov exponents for the torus map in equation (1)

evidence.quote: 2.5. Another Example Let f : T2 → T2 be defined by f(x,y ) = ( 2x +y− 1/(2π)c sin(2πx), x+y− 1/(2π)c sin(2πx) ). (1)
Open Problem 10.3: For c > 1 the map given in (1), has positive Lyapunov exponents on a set of positive measure?
